title: Michael Zheng Surprises at the US Open and Becomes a National Talking Point
seoTitle: Michael Zheng Surprises at the US Open
subtitle: The Chinese-American tennis player reaches the third round in his Grand Slam debut
excerpt: Recent Columbia graduate Michael Zheng advances to the US Open third round, becoming a focal point for tennis fans and experts in Brazil.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Michael Zheng, 22, reached the third round of the US Open in his first appearance in the main draw, generating great interest among Brazilian fans. The youngster, who recently graduated from Columbia with a degree in psychology, received a wild card and had already won two matches on the outer courts of Flushing Meadows.

How Zheng earned the wild card for the US Open

After becoming a two-time NCAA Singles champion in 2025, Zheng was chosen to receive a wild card for the US Open, having qualified for all three of the year's Grand Slams. He chose not to play in the US Open Collegiate Playoff, but his presence in all major competitions secured him the spot.

First victory and support from the university community

In the first round, Zheng defeated Hungary's Fabian Marozsan 6-4, 6-4, 6-2 on an outer court. The tennis player highlighted the energy of the crowd, comparing the atmosphere to that of a college match, with chants of support from the Columbia community and former teammates.

Heading to the third round: opponent and expectations

In his second match, Zheng faced lucky loser Yunchaokete Bu of China and advanced to the third round, where he will face France's Arthur Gea, a familiar opponent whom Zheng defeated twice in 2024. Zheng's former coach, Howie Endelman, highlighted the player's ability to adapt after multiple matchups.

Financial impact and ranking position

By qualifying for the third round, Zheng guarantees prize money that exceeds what he used to earn in Challenger tournaments by more than $290,000. His world ranking reached No. 88, a career-high, reflecting his rapid rise since being ranked outside the top 700 just 15 months ago.

Reaction among tennis fans in Brazil

Zheng's journey has caught the attention of Brazilian fans, who have been following his progress since his historic NCAA victory, where he became the first Ivy League player to win the title in over a century. Comments from players like 20th seed Tommy Paul reinforce the perception that Zheng could become a permanent contender on the professional circuit.

With information from ZooTennis, New York Post.
